Definition: to go away, hence, to disappear
BiblicalUsage: Azal means to go away, to disappear — like water running off. Moses says the Lord will judge his people and repent himself for his servants when he seeth that their power is gone, Job says the waters fail from the sea and the flood decayeth and drieth up, and Jeremiah says his people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit, going after vanity.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that everything that is not God disappears in the end — power gone, waters dried up, vanity proved empty. Only his mercy stays, and that is what I build on.
